messages.subject: second order sem raise the identification error however more complicated SEM model works fine
parts:
dear volunteers

I am doing a second order sem analysis. My full model works fine. However in order to report my results, I am following the two-steps approach. Once I tested the second order measurement model without the structural part. I am getting the following error
lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

Following is my structural model which works fine.
+ OI =~O1+O2+O3+O4+O5+O6+O7+O8
+ OD =~O9+O10+O11+O12
+ OM =~ OI + OD
+ SE = S1 +S2+S3
+ SE ~OM
+ '


This is my measurement model which raises errors.
model <-'
+ OI =~O1+O2+O3+O4+O5+O6+O7+O8
+ OD =~O9+O10+O11+O12
+ OM =~ OI + OD
+ '
> fit <- sem(model, data =verise2)  


Is it an expected behaviour because my second order latent variables is measured only by 2 variables? Maybe I am following an incorrect approach for two step approach

Regards.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: second order sem raise the identification error however more complicated SEM model works fine
parts:
You can understand identification of second order factor models by analogy to identification of first order factor models.  One heuristic for the identification of a congeneric (meaning, no cross-loadings and no correlated residuals) factor model is that the model is identified with two indicators, as long as the factor itself is correlated with something else.  In your larger model, SE is the “something else.”  SE is not present in the smaller model, and that is why identification fails there.

     The notion that “structural model” and “measurement model” are somehow separate is not entirely helpful.  There is one system of equations.  (Composite-based methods really do have two distinct sets of equations, but factor-based methods do not.)  Two step approaches to assessing identification are sufficient but not necessary—you can fail these rules, yet your whole model may still be identified.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: second order sem raise the identification error however more complicated SEM model works fine
parts:
On 11/24/2014 11:18 PM, Er. OU wrote:
> Ok! What I understood that if I prefer to use two-step approach. I could
> report it without second order by using the just correlations, As the
> following code, Their standard errors are also equal to the second order
> one which I am looking for.
>
> + OI =~O1+O2+O3+O4+O5+O6+O7+O8
> + OD =~O9+O10+O11+O12
>
> I have tested that and it worked fine.

If you prefer to keep an (equivalent) 2nd order model for the first
step, you can set the two factor loadings of the 2nd factor to 1.0:

OM =~ 1*OI + 1*OD

here, the estimated variance of OM will be the same as the covariance
between OI and OD in the 1st order model.

Yves.
